asr.full_text: Hello everyone my name is Catherine Gou and I'm the head of product for digital assets at Solana Foundation. Today here with me I have Roger from CrossMint with with me to talk about Solana Developer Platform. Roger welcome to the to the show how you doing? Thank you so much for having me doing great great great um you're the co-founder of CrossMint. Maybe tell us a little bit about yourself as well as well as what does CrossMint do? Yeah, sure. I'm Rodri, originally from Spain, as listeners will probably guess by my accent. My background is in engineering and then I work mostly on financial services during the last 10 years at McKinsey, start, investing, and so on. I started Crossmeant as a Zen Monastery about four years ago with my co-founder, Alfonso. I dropped out of school to join the monastery and somehow got distracted and that ended up being an issue at the company. A bit about what we do is we're a stablecoin platform we help primarily financial institutions and enterprises and fintechs integrate stablecoins on their flows. I also think of us as a online platform that includes things like wallet infrastructure both treasury and embedded wallets as well as on and off ramps and orchestration or put together into a cohesive platform that is targeted to those customer specifically. And so we serve customers typically in remittances or companies like money ground, which is a union, companies doing things like payroll, cross-border payments, NEO banks, and so on and so forth. That's awesome. I think this is a great segue to just focus a little bit more in terms of what does it mean to have enterprise grade infrastructure? What can cross mint bring to whether Western union of the world? What kind of bar they're looking for? As we're specifically as we're starting to integrate cross mint into SDP as well, how can we leverage these sort of infrastructures? Yeah, so there's a few things. The first one is around compliance. Obviously, deploying global stablecoin products has a lot of nuances across different geographies. Oftentimes, depending on the flows that the customer is interested in integrating, it has different licensing requirements. And so, what Pl platform provides is, number one, flexibility around the custody model. So customers can use our licenses for some of the flows, use our licenses in the places that they need to, and have all of that integrated into one single place. We have coverage for about 170 different countries depending on the on the table flow with our licenses and all of the infrastructure that we provide, has all of the different compliance tools that you need to deploy these programs in production. And also think of things like a email screening, travel rule compliance, transaction monitoring and so on. If they are having to go and figure out, hey, what are the specific rules for each of the geographies and integrating all the different tools to be able to deploy that live. All of those integrations come already native by default in the platform. So, companies don't have to worry about that. And then obviously, security is a key component to now. Especially for companies who are going to be started or moving, a lot of funds, then, obviously, that is this fundamental. That is on the wallet infrastructure it sells for some of the other flows. It's a critical component. And so, we are basically, whether it's through Dora compliance or something, and all of those things that's where the platform would be prepared in that regard to handle vast amounts of volume. I think also just maybe clicking through what's more exciting more cool about STP. I mean especially having you guys like design partner from day one. There's a lot of ambitions we want to achieve through STP, but through your lens, as you think about leveraging STP as sort of a piece of public infrastructure, truly, right? For Crossmen to reach more clients and also enable more use cases. What would you say are sort of the unique things you see on STP, whether it's for the current form of vWorld or like down the road, but would you like to see. Yeah. I mean, typically deploying a stable coin product is relatively complicated. And that I think a lot of clients, a lot of enterprises still even if they have like incipient blockchain and during teams, and so on there's still a lot of, whether it's like resources from a technical standpoint or support from a more like a strategic or ecosystem side. I think basically what the SDP does is basically they put together all of these different tools that you may need to deploy into one single page that is just much easier to use. And it has all these little support from Solana and behind, who has deployed similar programs at scale, across many different financial institutions, and so it does. It just like makes life's easier now for enterprises to start, at least piloting and in deploying some of these problems. I think it's very easy. We see a lot pretty frequently, clients sometimes get stuck in a design or prototype phase because of that fragmentation. And so I think this basically will help test and accelerate and make sure that they go live faster. Yeah, yeah, that cycled fast like is kind of a main ethos of what we're trying to achieve. And I think that's critical for a lot of the big institutions as they're trying to iterate on product ideas. I guess my last question, and this is just to kind of to end with a concrete example that you can walk through for the audience here, in which, you know, have a specific enterprise use case, whether that's remittance B2B or whatnot ... ...in which how to leverage crossments infrastructure exactly to achieve it. Maybe we can use like, let's say like a parable example. So let's take an example where you have a private company that is collecting funds from employers and they want to distribute those to our global workforce that is distributed around the world. So there's a few different models or components that they need to deploy this life. And so initially where you started the flow is such a company has certain Fiat assets on their bank account. So what we're going to do is we're going to create a tertiary wallet for them where they can basically manage their own digital assets and we're going to give them B to B on and off rams to be able to fund that treasury wallet so that they can access the Bitcoin. That is initial phase. The second one is like now they have stable coins. They want to start distributing them. And so that's where like our licensing infrastructure comes into play. So they can leverage our infrastructure to do payouts in about 170 different countries or so. So we coordinate all of that orchestration of many different payments to many different users. Then, for users who do not have wallets, we can create a wallet that the Sparrow Company can embed inside of their own application for users to receive funds in a way that's completely abstracted with their blockchain, and then, we can also do retail on and off ramps there so the users can actually withdraw funds back into fiat or continue to fund that wallet as needed. And then for the wallet, if they want to add additional financial services, things like cards, YIELD, tokenized stocks and so on and so forth, we have extensions to allow them to add all those different things without needing to spend a lot of engineering effort doing so. That is basically sort of a typical 1121, we're also adding our virtual accounts which basically allows users to get a bank account, unique bank account numbers in both the US and Europe, regardless of their location, obviously with disclaimers for sanction geography is not as shown, but basically we can provide non us and non European customers with, with Bridgel bank accounts where they can receive funds from third parties that allows say like a contractor, for example, in Colombia be able to get a payment from an employer or any you know type of third party in Europe and get that instantly as a domestic transaction getting somebody convert it into stable coins and appear on their wallet to be able to use. And so if you take a step back now, you look at the intereflow that basically provides a lot of different modules that allow you to build a scalable product, without needing to go crazy about finding vendors following from parts of the stack, which especially for an enterprise it has done a lot the cycle. actually on-line, but it's because it was a huge time that I lost the conversation and had some issues but then I was able to see some of the other people that were there to also, also have some kind of common issues and I think that's a fantastic lesson or something I've learned in the past. It's definitely an educational experience so I really appreciate it. And yeah, I know, to me that, what we really need is an online session to be able to share and chat with some of those people We work with you guys again across a spectrum of things including custody, rents, and many other things beyond that, as we're looking at, say, for example, on the trading side down the road. So, fantastic. Thank you very much, Rodrigue, for coming to the show, and we look forward to working with you guys.
